title: Connexions de Gauss-Manin et équations de Picard-Fuchs. Opération de Cartier : copies de tapuscrit annoté (s.d.), tiré à part (1981), notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context (§5 of a draft on Cartier operation and Gauss–Manin connection, c. 1972). Data: S of characteristic p; X/S smooth, or at least locally admitting a p-basis over the relative Frobenius twist X^{(p/S)}. L is an invertible O_X-module with a reference connection Δ0 relative to S. Δ0 is integrable and compatible with p-th powers, i.e. has zero p-curvature. Any other connection is Δ = Δ0 + ω with ω ∈ Γ(Ω^1_{X/S}).

Proposition, two parts.
(i) Δ is integrable iff dω = 0. The page notes this is standard and independent of characteristic. In higher rank, ω is End(E)-valued and the condition becomes dω + [ω,ω] = 0 (Maurer–Cartan).
(ii) Assume Δ is integrable. Then Δ has zero p-curvature (Θ_ξ^p = Θ_{ξ^p}) iff C̃ω = ω̃ ⊗ 1_Λ. Here C is the Cartier operator on closed 1-forms and ω̃ is the Frobenius-twisted form on X^{(p/S)}, pulled back.

Proof of (ii).
- The question is local, so take X = Spec B affine with a p-basis x_i, x_i^p = a_i, and D_i = ∂/∂x_i, so D_i^p = 0.
- The ring of differential operators generated by the D_i and scalars has generators D_i, x_i. Relations: [D_i,D_j] = 0, [x_i,x_j] = 0, [D_i,x_j] = δ_ij, x_i^p = a_i, D_i^p = 0.
- Hence compatibility with p-th powers reduces to the necessary conditions Θ_{D_i}^p = 0, and these are also sufficient.
- Write ω = Σ c_i dx_i, so Θ_{D_i} = Θ^0_{D_i} + c_i·id. The condition becomes (Δ_i^0 + c_i)^p = 0.
- Jacobson's formula, cited on the next page to Sém. Chevalley 58/59 exp. 6, gives (D+c)^p = D^p + c^p + D^{p-1}(c). With D^p = 0 the condition reads c_i^p + D_i^{p-1}c_i = 0 for all i.
- For closed ω one has C̃ω = −Σ D_i^{p-1}c_i (dx̃_i ⊗ 1) and ω̃ = Σ c_i^p (dx̃_i ⊗ 1).
- Hence ω̃ − C̃ω = Σ (c_i^p + D_i^{p-1}c_i)(dx̃_i ⊗ 1), which vanishes exactly when the conditions hold.

In modern terms: the p-curvature of d + ω is F*(ω̃ − Cω), the Cartier–Katz formula.

Marginal notes:
- define the obstruction to p-power compatibility intrinsically, as a section of Ω^1_{X/S} ⊗ End(E) attached to the connection; this is the p-curvature ψ;
- the statement is independent of the rank-1 hypothesis.

Purpose: to identify invertible sheaves with p-curvature-zero connections, i.e. descent data to X^{(p)} (next page, Cartier descent), with logarithmic differentials. This is Cartier's classical characterization: ω = df/f locally iff dω = 0 and Cω = ω.
errors: The higher-rank curvature formula 'dω + [ω,ω] = 0' is off by a convention factor. The standard form is dω + ω∧ω = 0, i.e. dω + ½[ω,ω] = 0. This is a harmless normalization slip.

Reducing p-power compatibility to the generators D_i is asserted ('on voit aisément') but not proved. It needs that ξ ↦ Θ_ξ^p − Θ_{ξ^p} is p-linear (additive and Frobenius-semilinear), which is Katz's/Deligne's lemma. The presentation of the algebra of differential operators alone does not immediately give it.

The sign in C̃ω = −Σ D_i^{p-1}c_i dx̃_i depends on the normalization of the Cartier operator. This is consistent with the standard identity C(f^p x^{p-1} dx) = f dx, but it is not checked on the page.

deep.surprise_reason: This is a careful, routine derivation of the known Cartier–Katz criterion (p-curvature of d+ω equals F*ω − Cω), published by Katz in 1970 and going back to Cartier. The margin's push for an intrinsic obstruction in Ω^1 ⊗ End(E) is just p-curvature. It is of historical interest only as evidence of Grothendieck working through this material himself.
transcription_corrections: The subscript in the first line is very likely O_{X^{(p/S)}} (relative Frobenius twist), not 'O_{X×S}': C̃ω = ω̃ ⊗_{O_{X^{(p/S)}}} 1_Λ.
'mais localisons[?]' is probably 'mais localement libre' or similar; the bracket concerns E of arbitrary rank.
The upper-left margin heading seems to read something like 'mal déduit de division des p-puiss.'; it is uncertain, and 'mal à droite' is unlikely.
In the margin formula, 'ω⊗p − ∫_{X/S}' is probably a garbled rendering of F*_{X/S}-pullbacks: something like F*ω̃ − F*C̃ω = F*_{X/S}(ω̃ − C̃ω).
